response:
It takes courage to reach out about this. Struggling with self-esteem and body image is incredibly common, but it is also very painful to feel like you do not like yourself. A great place to start finding help is by reaching out to a licensed therapist or counselor, particularly one who specializes in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) or body image issues. You can find professionals through online mental health directories, or by asking your primary care doctor for a referral. Support groups can also connect you with others facing similar challenges so you do not feel so alone.

In the meantime, try practicing self-compassion. When you notice negative thoughts about your image, gently ask yourself if you would speak to a friend that way. Focusing on what your body can do rather than just how it looks, and limiting time on social media accounts that make you feel inadequate, can also be helpful first steps toward building a kinder relationship with yourself.
